findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Surface in the parent plan (or cb2b's Ordering) that criterion 4's sync test requires the overlap epic's overlap_* removal story (09a8-5436-6b65-479c) to have landed first.
evidence: cb2b Approach: 'Equality is exact, so this depends on the overlap epic's removal story (granitic-realisable-dolphin, 09a8-5436-6b65-479c)'
Parent plan has no ordering/dependency note mentioning the overlap epic or 09a8
findings.finding: Cross-plan dependency gap: child cb2b's [llm] unknown-key sync test (criterion 4) depends on an out-of-epic story (overlap epic granitic-realisable-dolphin / 09a8-5436-6b65-479c) because its _LLM_KNOWN_KEYS exact-equality assertion would false-warn until that story removes the overlap_* keys. This dependency is internal to cb2b and is NOT surfaced in the parent plan's ordering or dependency narrative, so the parent cannot see that criterion 4's completion is gated on a sibling outside this epic.
scenarios: If the overlap epic's removal story has not landed, cb2b's sync test false-warns and criterion 4 cannot be verified
The parent-level reviewer, seeing only the epic's own children, has no visibility that criterion 4 is gated externally
findings.suggested_fix: Add a depends_on from cb2b to 09a8-5436-6b65-479c and note the external gate in the parent's ordering so criterion 4's prerequisite is explicit.

evidence: Plan: 'migrate 51 resolver-shim importers to rebar._ids' and 'repoint the 7 reducer/_processors.py re-exports across 9 modules'
Plan AC1: 'Checked by an AST importer census ... in each shim story.'

Repo shows module-attribute-access usage of this package's re-exports: src/rebar/reducer/_version.py:13 '(_processors.replay)' and :86 '(_processors.replay)' — a reference form an import-statement census does not enumerate.
findings.finding: S1a/S1b enumerate the resolver-shim (9 names from rebar._ids, 51 importers) and the reducer/_processors.py re-export (7 names, 9 modules) removal inventories, but the AC states each was derived by 'an AST importer census' — an import-statement scan, which is neither a find_referencing_symbols sweep nor a name-string grep. An import census finds `from X import Y`/`import X` but does not surface dynamic string imports (importlib.import_module) nor attribute-access use of the re-exported names through the module object.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, criterion 1: 'Checked by an AST importer census and `make verify` in each shim story.'
scenarios: An importer that uses `importlib.import_module('rebar._engine_support.resolver')` or references `_processors.<name>` via module-attribute access survives the import census, leaving a live reference to a deleted shim and a broken caller at runtime.
A string-based reference to one of the 7 re-exported processor names escapes the structural import scan and is not migrated.
findings.suggested_fix: For each removed name run find_referencing_symbols to get structural references, then grep the name as a string across src/, tests/, and scripts/ to catch dynamic imports and attribute-access uses; reconcile both into the per-story importer list.
